subject: Human Body
title: Spinal Cord Injuries
description: A short lesson to help you apply Spinal Cord Injuries.

hook.text: Sever the spinal cord at the neck and everything below goes silent. Arms, legs, and organs lose contact with the brain.

buildup.text: Higher injuries cause more paralysis. Neck injuries affect all four limbs. Lower injuries may spare the arms.

discovery.text: The cord can't regenerate in humans. Unlike skin or bone, central nervous tissue doesn't regrow naturally.

twist.text: Some animals can regenerate spinal cords. Salamanders regrow entire sections. Scientists study them for human therapies.

climax.text: Stem cell and electrical stimulation trials show early promise. Some paralyzed patients have regained limited movement.

punchline.text: The cord won't fix itself yet. Science is learning to help.

quiz.question: Why can't spinal cord injuries heal naturally?
options: The bone prevents access for repair
Central nervous tissue doesn't regenerate in humans
Blood can't reach the injury site
